body: # Advocacy Neurodiversity is a fact (the infinite variation in minds), a paradigm (no "right" way for a mind to work) and a movement (civil rights, inclusion & equality for neurodivergent folks). Psychology & psychiatry have a long record of ignoring this and causing harms to neurodivergent folks through pathologisation, eugenics, and institutionalisation. Some efforts towards increasing awareness and participatory research: ## Neurodiversity in academia A workshop at Princeton, co-organised with Mira Nencheva, Laura Murray and Laura Bustamante for the Princeton University Neurodiversity Collective ↗. History & background of the movement, from critical psychiatry and Mad Pride to neurodiversity; the harms, past and present; where academia is now (legislation, accommodations, stigma, the need to disclose); a panel on lived experience; and breakout rooms on participatory research and teaching. Slides ↗ are here, borrow freely. ## Neurodiversity resource guide for scientists Written with Charlie Rodriguez-Deliz and the Scientist Action and Advocacy Network ↗ (ScAAN), by neurodivergent scientists for the broader scientific community: what neurodiversity and disability mean, disability rights as civil rights, why this concerns you as a scientist, community-based participatory research, identity-first language, and re-evaluating interventions like ABA. PDF ↗. ## #StopTheShock campaign The Judge Rotenberg Center in Massachusetts still uses electric shock devices on disabled residents. The FDA banned the devices in 2020; a federal court overturned the ban in 2021; Congress restored the FDA's authority in 2022; the FDA re-proposed the ban in 2024 and missed its own deadline to finalise it in 2026. Campaign page ↗ and fact sheet ↗ from the Autistic Self Advocacy Network. ## Season of the Bitch, ep. 185: Freud is the worst A podcast episode ↗ on the history of psychology & psychiatry: Freud, the pathologisation of Black, queer, trans and neurodivergent people, the carceral mental health system, and non-carceral alternatives (peer support, Mad Pride, the neurodiversity movement). Resources in the show notes.

Hi, I'm Sashank! I'm a research scientist with 10+ years of experience studying the failure modes of intelligent systems. Currently, I work on model behaviour & alignment of open-weight models at **Reflection** ↗. Previously, I lead the research team at Atla training general-purpose evaluators ↗, prior to which I was at Limbic building safety guardrails ↗ for mental health applications. Before that, I was a postdoc at Princeton studying continual learning failures ↗ in psychotherapy, following my PhD in computational neuroscience studying lapses ↗ in decision-making. I enjoy making music and writing poems ↗. email: firstname[dot]lastname[at]gmail.com

# Poetry A few selected poems. The rest, going back to 2011, are on wordpress ↗. ## sooth & nail

hold fast my skin,
contain what’s within me;
don’t open up steaming
on water or whim

something beneath
fast pulsing or breathing,
stuck under a nail bed
of hands or my feet

sitting at home
but home once forgotten,
I peer inside of my being
fibre and bone

structured and dry,
a plan of a plan I see
patiently screaming
this mouth or an eye

something distracts
there in the ground I keep
plastic syringe I must
throw away fast

was it not pain?
no, tenderness at worst
exposed and sweating
but fearless frame

pores open wide
visceral feeling
inviting me gently to
see what’s inside

see sooth, and say
what this partial membrane
holds within and without
not seance but song

clear as the night
watery organs
not full moon, not half dog
but sobering light

two birds, two stones
council of matriarchs
skeleton woman
from dreams long ago

what did she say?
nothing at all at first,
looks of assurance
I’m not going away

and in this dream
not in a dungeon, no
sitting up, I awake
surrogate stream

hold fast my skin,
I know what’s within me;
a channel, a river bed
water and whim.

## drip.

Two drops on a mossy brick
Surrounded by an impossibly vast expanse
The storm won’t let up, a river in spate
Towering blocks raring to fall.

Two drops slither down in synchronous delight
Trying to not lose themselves
In the deluge, down the brick walls
Occasionally stopping on a blade of grass.

Two drops find a rhythm unlikely
Circling, here-a-stopping, there-a-dropping
Following one another down the plunge
Night falls unbeknownst to anyone.

Two drops join the collective din
Of ten billion drops passing through the wind
Soon to swim back up the sky
And form ten billion more.

I don’t get giddy when I breathe
in but every breath that I
steal from under your nose
while we fold up somewhere
is a contact high.

## Forgotten.

Forgotten words I didn’t say
Forgotten, or just yesterday’s
Soon it will be another
Forgotten doubt

Forgotten dreams I didn’t dream
Misremembered, and better still
Missed memories
I dream without

For gathering in my dusty eye
Stormy day within, without
Is there a chance
Of sudden drought

Forgotten birds, they didn’t mind
Flew high, far, free, and light
Let the wind carry
Them away

## ephemera.

I catch my reflection in the dusty window pane of a passing train,
Preen, vain, window, pain;
Staring, starring, stardust too caught up in the brilliance of its own fast burn;
Mesmerized, vaporized.
A moment of recognition, of self, of identity, and immediately of vanity
Self, selfish. Consciousness? No, how can I be conscious when I am so confident?
I confide in myself; sometimes this makes me feel powerful, sometimes overpowered
Not conscious of myself, not conscious at all, only consummate, luscious, copious
A flick of the hair, like a comet’s tail
A tilt of the hip, like a
Beckoning (come hither)
Echo
The sounds of my own voice
Writhing about, writing about myself
Gotta get it out.
Why is there such a fine line between self love and self loathing?
To be loved by myself is intoxicating, overbearing
Love, self.

Dollop of honey,
Slow teardrop, sweet, sour memory
Of a thousand trips.

# Agentic failure modes

Atla, 2025 · Reflection, current

Evaluating multi-step agent trajectories is a bottleneck: human annotation of a single trajectory can take hours, so teams use LLM judges to critique agents at the process & outcome level, and the soundness of those critiques mostly goes unmeasured. Counsel ↗ is the first public meta-evaluation dataset for agentic tasks: process-level critiques from open-weight LLM judges on τ-bench (customer support agents) and DA-Code (coding agents), with 1.13k human annotations of whether each flagged error is spot on, right location but poor reasoning, or shouldn't have been flagged (Krippendorff's α = 0.78). More capable judges and more reasoning effort both improve agreement with humans. The best judge agrees with humans on *where* the error is ~88% of the time, and on *why* only ~65%. At Atla I also spearheaded a company-wide initiative to build inference-time critics for policy evaluation & improvement of agents, grounded in RL theory, in collaboration with Cohere. **Papers** - **Pisupati**, Broomfield, Choi, Calvi, Wang, Engeler, Bartolo, Lewis (2026). Counsel: a meta-evaluation dataset for agentic tasks ↗. *arXiv*. Dataset & tech report ↗, permissively licensed.

# Anxiety, addiction & continual learning

Princeton Neuroscience Institute, 2019–2023 · postdoc with Yael Niv

Why do some beliefs and action policies resist updating? In the latent-cause framework, the brain infers which hidden cause is generating its current experience, and a new experience either updates an existing cause or creates a new one. Get that wrong in one direction and a fear never extinguishes; in the other, a drug association survives abstinence and relapse looks like chasing the first high. Both are failures of continual learning. In the Niv lab ↗ I built hierarchical Bayesian nonparametric models of human inductive biases for aversive continual learning, to identify where someone's learning has stalled, in order to deliver adaptive and personalised psychotherapy. With Isabel Berwian and colleagues we also wrote up how computational models of learning map onto what CBT actually does (exposure, cognitive restructuring). **Papers** - Berwian, Hitchcock, **Pisupati**, Schoen, Niv (2025). Using computational models of learning to advance cognitive behavioral therapy ↗. *Communications Psychology*. - **Pisupati**, Langdon, Konova, Niv (2024). The utility of a latent-cause framework for understanding addiction phenomena ↗. *Addiction Neuroscience*. - **Pisupati**\*, Berwian\*, Chiu, Ren, Niv (2023). Human inductive biases for aversive continual learning: a hierarchical Bayesian nonparametric model ↗. *PMLR (CoLLAs)*. - Bedder, **Pisupati**, Niv (2023). Modelling rumination as a state-inference process. *CogSci*. - **Pisupati**, Niv (2022). The challenges of lifelong learning in biological and artificial systems ↗. *Trends in Cognitive Sciences*. - **Pisupati** et al. (2022). Why do some beliefs and action policies resist updating? ↗ *RLDM*. - **Pisupati**, Langdon, Niv (2021). Two factors underlying maladaptive inference of causal structure can drive resistance to extinction in anxiety. *Biological Psychiatry* (abstract).

# Lapses & exploration

Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory, 2014–2019 · PhD with Anne Churchland

Perceptual decision-makers make errors even on the easiest trials. These "lapses" are usually treated as noise and fit away with a nuisance parameter. In a multisensory rate-discrimination task in rats, we showed that lapses instead reflect a strategic trade-off between exploiting known rewarding actions and exploring uncertain ones: changing the reward magnitude or probability of one action changed only the lapses associated with that action, as the model predicted, and inactivating posterior striatum or secondary motor cortex changed lapses in a modality-specific way. Lapses carry information about action values, and about the animal's uncertainty, that the standard models throw away. (Press: In mapping mistakes, a window to the inner mind ↗, Simons Foundation.) **Papers** - **Pisupati**, Chartarifsky-Lynn, Khanal, Churchland (2021). Lapses in perceptual decisions reflect exploration ↗. *eLife*. - Odoemene, **Pisupati**, Nguyen, Churchland (2018). Visual evidence accumulation guides decision-making in unrestrained mice ↗. *Journal of Neuroscience*. - **Pisupati**, Chartarifsky, Churchland (2016). Decision activity in parietal cortex: leader or follower? ↗ *Trends in Cognitive Sciences*. - **Pisupati** (2019). A value-based explanation for lapses in perceptual decisions. PhD thesis, Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory.

# Mental health guardrails

Limbic, 2023–2024

At Limbic ↗ I was an ML scientist building clinical AI across the mental healthcare pathway, under medical device regulation. **Scalable oversight.** Fine-tuned evaluator models that achieved ~15% better alignment with humans than GPT-4o, for scalable evaluation and guardrailing of LLM agents in a real-world safety-critical setting. Bandit algorithms to optimise prompts on those evaluation metrics (>29 iterations in <3 months) while minimising user exposure to risk. **Steerable agents.** LLM agents grounded in clinical expertise (RAG, fine-tuned classifiers, guardrails), preferred 94% of the time over GPT-4 by domain experts, and translated into production in ~3 months with compliance, engineering and product. **Papers** - Rollwage, McFadyen, Juchems, Balogh, **Pisupati**, et al. (2026). A cognitive layer architecture to support large-language model performance in psychotherapy interactions ↗. *Nature Medicine*. - Rollwage, Juchems, **Pisupati**, et al. (2024). The Limbic Layer: transforming large language models into clinical mental health experts. *OSF preprint*. - Rollwage, **Pisupati**, et al. (2023). Real-world evaluation of an ML decision support system for mental health assessments. *Computational Psychiatry Conference*.

# Open-weight judges

Atla, 2024–2025 · Reflection, current

At Atla ↗ I led the research & technical reports for two evaluation models, fine-tuned on a combined SFT + DPO objective, that achieve state-of-the-art performance across 11 benchmarks: - Selene 1 Mini ↗, an open-weights small eval model that beats GPT-4o-mini and other small models, with >30K downloads on HuggingFace. - Selene 1 ↗, a large LLM-as-a-judge that beats frontier models including Claude 3.5 Sonnet & o1. I also built the internal tooling for data curation, filtering and automated model analysis that cut our time to train & evaluate models by ~5x. At Reflection this continues as generative reward models. **Papers** - Alexandru, Calvi, Broomfield, Golden, Dai, Leys, Burger, Bartolo, Engeler, **Pisupati**, Drane, Park (2025). Atla Selene Mini: a general purpose evaluation model ↗. *arXiv*. - **Pisupati** et al. (2026). Counsel: a meta-evaluation dataset for agentic tasks ↗. *arXiv*.
